shortName: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The School of Medicine is committed to maintaining a varied student body and community. We believe such diversity is invaluable in a case-based curriculum heavily based on small group and interactive learning. The school hosts a premedical summer enrichment program, the Prologue to Medicine Program, for admitted students who believe they would benefit from a preview of the medical school curriculum. Following admission, a broad range of support services and programs are available to enhance academic success.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A break from the curriculum may be granted for personal, academic, or medical reasons. Requesting a leave of absence must follow the policies and procedures outlined in the student handbook and meet approval requirements. For details, please refer to www.medstudentaffairs.pitt.edu/handbook/documents/LEAVEOFABSENCEPOLICYNEW.pdf
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The wide variety of extracurricular activities available reflects students’ diverse, creative, educational, and recreational interests and pursuits. There are more than 60 student groups listed at medgroups.pitt.edu, including department-sponsored interest groups like Critical Care Medicine, Anesthesiology, Plastic Surgery, and others.

Students can participate in community service with the Birmingham Free Clinic or Operation Safety Net, which provides health care for Pittsburgh’s unhoused population. Pitt hosts active chapters of prominent national organizations. Popular Pitt activities include the annual talent show, and Scope and Scalpel, the graduating class’s musical theater production.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The School of Medicine is located in an urban setting on the University of Pittsburgh’s main campus in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, within proximity of multiple hospitals and the University’s five other health sciences schools. 

Also home to Pitt’s close collaborator Carnegie Mellon University, this section of the city includes the Carnegie Museum of Art, the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens, parks, shops and dozens of restaurants. 
 
Approximately 307,000 people call the city of Pittsburgh home, and the population of the 7-county region is approximately 2.4 million. Pittsburgh is vibrant, safe, and affordable. Its 90 eclectic neighborhoods feature the amenities of a large city with small-town civility.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus apartments for medical, dental and pharmacy students are available: https://www.pc.pitt.edu/housing-services/university-owned-housing/darragh-street-apartments
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine (UPSOM) seeks to build a varied and vibrant community, where everyone feels acknowledged, respected and valued. The curriculum includes a new clinical elective on LGBTQ health care. The Medical Student Pride Alliance offers a mentorship program to pair LGBTQ+ students with physicians. PRIDE Health is an LGBTQ group for UPMC and the University of Pittsburgh Schools of the Health Sciences.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Please refer to our website: https://www.medadmissions.pitt.edu/admissions/you-apply/frequently-asked-questions for more information regarding our technical standards and accommodations through University Disability Services.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Mental health resources include psychiatrists, therapists and student advocates. A well-being committee made up of students and faculty members meets monthly to create schoolwide initiatives for the students. The School of Medicine offers students a host of wellness activities, including therapy dogs, a pumpkin carving contest, healthy eating snack weeks, a Valentine's Day gratitude wall, ice skating, yoga, and more.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The School of Medicine fosters a culture of health and wellness, offering students access to a dedicated mental health team of licensed therapists, clinical psychiatrists, an advisory dean, coach, and learning specialist to support academic and personal success. Each student also receives a student mentor through the BIG/Little Program. The student-only sixth floor of the School of Medicine’s West Wing also provides a student haven, featuring a quiet room for catching a snooze, group study spaces and a lounge with billiards, a Wii and more. Among many clubs and activities, Pitt Med students can join Scope and Scalpel, a beloved Pitt Med theatrical production tradition. The shows, produced by fourth-year students, are inspired by pop culture and parody their medical school experience with titles like “Back to the Suture” and “West Wing Story.”
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Although the School of Medicine is located in an urban area and most of our healthcare clinical sites are located on campus or easily accessible by public transportation, an automobile may be necessary. Our Clerkship Directors have had to expand clinical care sites to the greater Pittsburgh region to better serve your education and provide you with a broad range of patient populations and care models. Also, public transportation may not be an option for early morning or late-night shifts.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Academic Development Office assists students with individual peer tutoring, academic counseling, screening for undiagnosed learning difficulties, USMLE review, career development, and counseling.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group instruction, problem-based learning activities, computer-based study, community visits, and clinical experiences
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students are required to rotate through eight required clerkships, three clinical focus courses, and an acting internship beginning with the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Three Rivers Curriculum combines social medicine, leadership, interprofessional education and clinical reasoning with in-depth studies in health sciences to cultivate graduates with diverse skills, clinical competence, and a commitment to community engagement and health equity. 

First-year learning is case-based. Students develop foundational knowledge in anatomy, immunology, genetics, microbiology and other disciplines. Students also develop core clinical skills and experience primary care ambulatory settings, where they learn how to establish a patient/doctor relationship and develop techniques for physical examinations. 

In the second year, students complete the Foundations phase and have six weeks of dedicated study time for the Step 1 exam. They then begin to participate in clerkships and gain essential patient care experience. 

In their third and fourth years, students concentrate on clinical knowledge, skills and specialty planning as they begin their transition into residency. 

The curriculum incorporates simulation training for hands-on experiences and learning clinical procedures. Specialized streams, akin to minors, enable students to concentrate on advocacy, innovation or leadership.

In addition to case-based learning, students participate in a mentored, longitudinal scholarly research project, which provides laboratory-based or clinical research, health policy, epidemiology, and comparative effectiveness research opportunities. The curriculum’s Longitudinal Alliance Program focuses on connecting a student with a patient in the student’s first year of medical school. Additionally, the Community Alliance Program enhances students’ abilities to address social determinants of health in their future careers.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
Approximately 35 percent of School of Medicine graduates enter a residency under the umbrella of primary care. One of Pitt’s unique opportunities is Operation Safety Net, a program where students bring primary care to the city’s homeless population.

Our new Primary Care Accelerated Track (PCAT) is a joint program between the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine (UPSOM) and UPMC Medical Education (residency programs) is for eager, innovative, compassionate and skilled students who are committed to the primary care fields of pediatrics, family medicine, and internal medicine. Accepted students will finish medical school in three years and be eligible for one of UPMC’s primary care residency programs if all requirements are met, including clinical competence, USMLE success, and general maturation. Please visit: www.omed.pitt.edu/primary-care-accelerated-track-pcat for more information.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Since 1998, the University of Pittsburgh, led by the School of Medicine, has ranked among the top 10 recipients of National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding, underscoring its research stature. 

At the School of Medicine, areas of research focus include the biology of aging; neuroscience; vision and vision restoration; genome stability and tumorigenesis; vascular, developmental, structural, computational, and systems biology; comparative effectiveness research; immunology; cancer virology; and clinical research and clinical trials, among others.

As part of the curriculum, all medical students at the University of Pittsburgh engage in a mentored longitudinal research project, which provides traditional laboratory-based or clinical research training, as well as health policy, epidemiology, and comparative effectiveness research opportunities.

medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Completion of a longitudinal research project of personal interest to the student. https://www.omed.pitt.edu/curriculum/longitudinal-research-project
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Through UPSOM's affiliation with the UPMC health care system ( www.upmc.com ), students have clinical, educational, and research opportunities in virtually every medical specialty.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine excels in basic science research, clinical and translational research, curricular development, and clinical care, with more than 2,000 full-time faculty and a core group of master educators. The University, led by the School of Medicine, has consistently remained within the top 10 recipients of National Institutes of Health Funding since 1998, underscoring its research stature. The school’s global collaborations connect Pittsburgh with China, India, Italy, Kazakhstan, France, and other nations. Its curriculum blends innovative teaching with staple techniques and supports specialized degree programs and in-depth studies. All medical students engage in a four-year longitudinal research project, which provides laboratory-based, clinical, and other forms of fundamental research experience. Through UPMC (the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center), students complete clinical training at top-tier hospitals with diverse patient populations.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Pitt Med's mission is to improve the health and well-being of individuals, communities and populations through cutting-edge research, innovative educational programs in medicine and biomedical science, and leadership in academic medicine. We strive to implement this mission with the highest professional and ethical standards.  Our commitment is to foster an environment that enables all students, faculty, staff and the communities we serve to develop to their fullest potential.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Applicants must send either 1 Committee Letter or 3 Individual Letters (5 letters maximum).
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We require three recommendations at a minimum or a committee letter (5 letters maximum). The committee letter should be buttressed with individual letters of recommendation. We prefer three letters of recommendation from professors or important mentors (such as research mentors). The best are letters from those who know the applicant well and can comment on our selection factors ( https://www.medadmissions.pitt.edu/admissions/you-apply/selection-factors ). Supplemental recommendations from the supervisors or peers of extracurricular activities or work positions are encouraged as well. Please visit: ( https://www.medadmissions.pitt.edu/admissions/you-apply/letters-recommendation ) for more information.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Includes a virtual greeting, a virtual faculty interview, a virtual medical student interview, and a virtual closing session.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: A virtual faculty interview and medical student interview are required.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The UPSOM Admissions Committee will continue to implement a comprehensive admissions process by combining multiple sources to gauge applicants’ knowledge, skills and attributes. This approach will evaluate a candidate's educational history and accomplishments, academic rigor of degrees and course work, performance on the MCAT standardized exam, leadership qualities, exposure to the medical field and career, participation in research activities, and a commitment to community service (paid, volunteer, altruistic, special interest, etc.).

Please note the following information and policies:

1. Online course work for prerequisites and labs are accepted and all course work must be completed at a regional accredited academic institution recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (undergraduate, graduate, post-baccalaureate, community college).
2. Traditional grading systems are encouraged; however, the Committee will accept Pass / Fail (Pass / No Credit, Satisfactory / Unsatisfactory) for prerequisite course work. **Students participating in our Special Programs (Guarantee Admit – GAP and the Summer Premedical Academic Enrichment Early Assurance – SPAEP EA) MUST obtain letter grades for ALL required prerequisite course work. When deciding whether to use an alternate or traditional grading system, you should select the option that is best for your application.
3. Online degrees will be accepted with an additional year of in-person instruction at a regionally accredited institution recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation within the United States and Canada.
4. MCAT score considered as it becomes available. Committee will only consider the highest score taken within the 3-year period prior to matriculation. 
5. Letters of Recommendation reviewed as they become available. The best letters are from those who know the applicant well and can comment on the competencies considered in a holistic evaluation process.

Please visit our Admissions web site, https://www.medadmissions.pitt.edu , for the most up-to-date information.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The scores achieved by an applicant on this national test give the Committee some indication of the applicant’s intellectual achievement. The MCAT must be taken no more than three years prior to application. MCAT scores are required of all applicants (unless specified within a special program affiliation).
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: No minimum undergraduate GPA for consideration but the Admissions Committee wants to see an improved and upward trajectory in academic performance in order to assess academic risk for the rigors of the medical school curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: No minimum number of credit hours to be eligible for consideration.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: All of those who matriculate at University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine must have an undergraduate degree which includes at least one year of post-secondary education in the United States or Canada. The Admissions Committee will consider any prerequisite course work completed at a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: The Admissions Committee will review and encourage applicants to submit letters of intent, explaining their reason(s) for wanting to attend UPSOM. Updates or achievements to an applicant’s submitted materials can be submitted through the application portal. Submissions are restricted to once prior to interview invitation, once after interviewing and once after a waitlist decision is rendered.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Please refer to our website: https://www.medadmissions.pitt.edu/admissions/you-apply/policies-restrictions regarding our Policy on Technical Standards for the Admission, Retention, and Graduation of Applicants and Medical Students.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Financial Aid Office assists students in securing funding needed for medical school and helps students understand the financial aid process. It takes great pride in getting to know its students personally and understanding each individual's financial situation. The office provides one-on-one meetings to help arrange financing throughout the four years of medical school, as well as ongoing debt counseling to help manage financial obligations. Financial aid resources available include need-based scholarships, unsubsidized loans, graduate PLUS loans, external scholarships, and various service-based programs. To be considered for financial aid, financial data from students, spouses, and parents must be submitted in a timely manner ( www.medadmissions.pitt.edu/financial-aid/ ).

medSchoolPrograms.info: The MD/PhD program ( www.mdphd.pitt.edu ) provides students with clinical knowledge and doctoral work in basic science, engineering, or public health at either Pitt or neighboring Carnegie Mellon University. Except for the MD/PhD program, combined degree programs are not offered directly through the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine. Students seeking a dual degree (an MD with a MBA, JD, MPH, or a MA in biomedical ethics) can contact other schools directly about applying and the curriculum. UPSOM students can also devote a full year to research and enrichment courses through either the Clinical Scientist Training Program ( www.icre.pitt.edu/cstp/index.html ) or the Physician Scientist Training Program ( www.pstp.pitt.edu ). The CSTP lets students further their mentored scholarly projects in clinical research during a fifth year of training. The PSTP provides two summers and a fifth year of lab-based training, preparing students for careers in academic medicine.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Doris Duke Foundation Academy for Clinical Research

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Qualified applicants who have identified a mentor within Pitt’s Schools of the Health Sciences and have been admitted to UPSOM are eligible to apply to the Pitt Med Research Experience for Pre-matriculants program ( PREP https://researchprograms.medschool.pitt.edu/about/pitt-med-research-experience-prematriculants ). The PREP program provides an accelerated research experience prior to matriculating into medical school. 

While in medical school, students can cultivate their enthusiasm for a particular aspect of medicine through Streams ( Streams – https://www.omed.pitt.edu/streams ), which supplement and complement the required core curriculum and enable further exploration of potential career plans. Three stream categories—advocate, innovator and leader—each encompass areas of focus, such as population health, entrepreneurship and education.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The Primary Care Accelerated Track (PCAT) was created as a joint program between the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine (UPSOM) and UPMC Medical Education to meet the growing need for primary care physicians across the country. This program allows accepted students to finish medical school in just three years and be eligible to enter one of UPMC’s primary care residency programs if all requirements are met.
medSchoolMdPathway.spotAvailable: There are 7 spots available in PCAT: 3 in Family Medicine (one at UPMC St. Margaret, one at UPMC Shadyside, and one at UPMC McKeesport), 2 in Internal Medicine at the Internal Medicine Residency Program of UPMC, and 2 in Pediatrics at the Pediatric Residency Program at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: This competitive program expects applicants to demonstrate not only the usual UPSOM prerequisites (academic excellence, service/extracurricular, commitment to medicine, teamwork, leadership ability, and resilience), but also special qualities that predict success in primary care, including commitment to a chosen primary care specialty, maturity, compassion/empathy, reflective ability, ability to form ongoing relationships, interest in working with underserved communities, and flexibility.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Applicants must go through the usual admissions process with UPSOM. If invited to interview, the PCAT application (which includes a special essay and identification of the specialty track of interest) becomes available. A selection committee at each residency program reviews the applications and invites appropriate candidates to interview virtually by specialty. Virtual Interview Days take place in February or March. Each program ranks candidates and offers are extended.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Admitted students will match within one of the following residencies after completing 3 years of their medical training: UPMC St. Margaret Family Medicine Residency, UPMC Shadyside Family Medicine Residency, UPMC McKeesport Family Medicine Residency, Pediatric Residency Program at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, or Internal Medicine Residency Program of UPMC.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students
medSchoolMdPathway.resAdditionalInfo: The Primary Care Accelerated Track gets primary care physicians into the community faster, where they are sorely needed. Program highlights include: Summer instruction and research experience tailored to Primary Care; Hands on experience with patients from the start of medical school and in a longitudinal fashion; Excellent mentorship at both the med school and residency levels; and a built in community from the start.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants are placed on the waitlist depending on Committee ranking. Applicants will be taken off the waitlist as seats in the class become available.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: All of those who matriculate at University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine must have an undergraduate degree which includes at least one year of post secondary education in the United States or Canada. Acceptance of courses taken at foreign universities is determined individually at the discretion of the Associate Dean of Admissions and Financial Aid. We will accept AP credit if that credit was awarded by your college/university and the course credit granted appears on your transcript. College Board’s College-Level Examination Program (CLEP) credits are not accepted. In examining your candidacy, the pre-requisites for the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine will be required. Substitution for required premedical coursework is granted at the discretion of the Associate Dean of Admissions on a case-by-case basis. Specific questions should be directed to the admissions office and proper details and documentation will need to be provided.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are selected from a broad base of undergraduate and graduate institutions and must have completed at least a bachelor’s degree. Selection is based on evidence of academic preparation, competitive standardized test scores, sustained participation in community and extracurricular activities, previous employment preparation, medically related experiences, and personal qualities and skills that demonstrate the applicant's motivation and suitability for a career in medicine. Some of these qualities include, but are not limited to, integrity, maturity, strong interpersonal skills, professionalism, strong oral and written communication skills, creativity, capacity for improvement, a willingness to participate in research activities, and evidence of leadership. All applicants are considered without regard to race, color, religion, ethnicity, national origin, age, gender, sexual orientation, marital, veteran, or disabled status.
